text:
Predicates:
Hydrocarbon(x) ::: x is a hydrocarbon.
Alkane(x) ::: x is an alkane.
Organic(x) ::: x is an organic compound.
Chemical(x) ::: x is a chemical compound.
ContainsCarbon(x) ::: x contains carbon.
ContainsOneElement(x) ::: x contains only one element.
Mixture(x) ::: x is a mixture.
Premises:
∀x (Hydrocarbon(x) → Organic(x)) ::: All hydrocarbons are organic compounds.
∀x (Alkane(x) → Hydrocarbon(x)) ::: All alkanes are hydrocarbons.
∀x (Organic(x) → Chemical(x)) ::: All organic compounds are chemical compounds.
∀x (Organic(x) → ContainsCarbon(x)) ::: All organic compounds contain carbon.
¬∃x (Chemical(x) ∧ ContainsOneElement(x)) ::: No chemical compounds contain only one element.
(Mixture(x) ∧ Chemical(x) ∧ ContainsOneElement(x)) ∨ ¬(Mixture(x) ∧ Chemical(x)) ::: The mixture either both is a chemical compound and contains only one element, or neither.
Conclusion:
Alkane(x) ∧ ContainsCarbon(x) ::: The mixture is an alkane and contains carbon.
